executive_narrative.title: FS Demo: Evidence Before Activation — Turning a Loaded Estate into a Governed AI Portfolio
executive_narrative.thesis: FS Demo has assembled the raw material for a bank-wide AI program — a fully-owned application estate, a rich book of regulated functions, and eighteen named initiatives with headline value signals — but almost none of it is yet finance-approved or control-linked. The governing argument is that the constraint on value is not idea supply; it is evidence, ownership, and control linkage. Leadership should treat the next two quarters as an evidence-and-accountability sprint that converts a directional portfolio into two or three defensible, in-production workflows, rather than launching the full slate at once.
executive_narrative.narrative_arc: The enterprise is a regulated, multi-line regional bank operating consumer and commercial banking, cards and payments, wealth, treasury, and financial crimes under strong oversight. Its technology estate is broad and, unusually, every application carries a named owner. Yet the initiative book — fraud, AML triage, SAR drafting, contact-center assist, credit spreading, Customer 360 — sits at planning-grade with no baselines, no realized savings, and no line to certified data products or controls. Industry patterns for regulated banking make the sequence unambiguous: model-risk gating, lineage, and reviewer controls come before scale. FS Demo is ahead on ownership hygiene and idea generation but behind on the evidence and control spine that lets any of these move to production. The path forward narrows the slate, assigns data-product and model accountability, and proves value on the fraud and AML workflows where the industry pattern and internal signal both point.
strategic_agenda: Narrow eighteen initiatives to two or three evidence-backed workflows and fund those to production.
Assign data-product ownership, model-risk accountability, and control attestation for every candidate before scale.
Establish finance-approved baselines so headline value signals become defensible business cases.
Sequence payments and Customer 360 work behind their core and lineage dependencies rather than in parallel.
strategic_tensions: Broad idea pipeline and headline value versus zero finance-approved baselines to defend any of it.
Complete application ownership versus unassigned data-product, model, and control accountability.
Pressure to demonstrate AI breadth versus regulatory requirement to gate on model risk and lineage first.
Vendor-rich estate that accelerates capability versus unlinked SLA, exit-right, and dependency exposure.

industry_comparison.pattern: Model-risk gate before bank AI scale
industry_comparison.specifics: The initiative book reaches production-grade ambition across fraud, AML, and credit, but model-risk accountability and SR 11-7-style evidence are not yet assigned or linked to the candidates. The bank is at idea maturity while the pattern requires a model-risk gate before any scale decision.

industry_comparison.pattern: Payments value gated by core and sanctions dependencies
industry_comparison.specifics: Payments and wire workflows depend on core banking and sanctions-screening platforms that show incomplete integration and lineage evidence. Payments value cannot be claimed until those upstream dependencies are certified, which they are not.

industry_comparison.pattern: AML false-positive reduction with review controls
industry_comparison.specifics: AML alert triage and false-positive reduction is a named initiative with a clear reviewer role in the estate, matching the pattern's shape. It sits at parity on intent but needs reviewer-control linkage and a false-positive baseline to move ahead.

industry_comparison.pattern: Financial Services Demo comparable transformation play 1
industry_comparison.specifics: The comparable-play library confirms fraud and financial-crimes automation as the standard first regulated-bank AI move; FS Demo's strongest value signal aligns to exactly this play, so it is at parity on selection and behind only on evidence.

material_gaps.statement: No finance-approved baseline, realized saving, or ROI exists for any current AI or modernization initiative.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Every headline value signal in the portfolio is undefendable in a board or regulator setting until a baseline is agreed with Finance; without it, the program cannot claim benefit or prioritize credibly.

material_gaps.statement: Data-product ownership, model-risk accountability, and control attestation are unassigned across the candidate workflows.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Regulated AI cannot pass a model-risk gate without a named accountable owner per model and per data product; this is the single largest blocker to moving anything to production.

material_gaps.statement: Regulatory-reporting, AML-reviewer, and fair-lending controls are not linked to certified data products or systems.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Unlinked controls mean the bank cannot demonstrate that an AI-assisted decision was governed, exposing it to supervisory and fair-lending challenge precisely where AI is most valuable.

material_gaps.statement: Core banking, payments, fraud, AML, and risk platforms operate with incomplete integration and lineage evidence.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Customer 360 and payments value both depend on trustworthy cross-system lineage; without it, the foundation initiatives cannot underwrite the workflow initiatives that sit on top of them.

material_gaps.statement: Vendor obligations — SLA linkage, invoice variance, exit rights — are not connected to the systems and workflows that depend on them.
material_gaps.why_it_matters_to_leadership: A vendor-rich estate concentrates delivery and concentration risk; leadership cannot manage renewal leverage or resilience without linking contracts to the critical workflows they underpin.

material_advantages.statement: Every application in the estate carries a named owner, captured directly on the source record.
material_advantages.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Complete application-ownership coverage removes a common first blocker to governed change; accountability for run health and architecture standards already exists to build on.

material_advantages.statement: The initiative pipeline is broad and correctly targets the highest-value regulated-bank plays — fraud, financial crimes, and contact-center assist.
material_advantages.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Selection risk is low; the bank has already identified the right first moves, so leadership can focus on evidence and sequencing rather than discovery.

material_advantages.statement: Functions, sponsors, and technology owners are already mapped to initiatives through the relationship evidence.
material_advantages.why_it_matters_to_leadership: Sponsor and owner linkage for named initiatives gives leadership a running start on accountability and change adoption once evidence gates are cleared.

material_advantages.statement: The regulated operating model is fully articulated across consumer, commercial, cards, payments, wealth, treasury, and financial crimes.
material_advantages.why_it_matters_to_leadership: A clear function map lets leadership target AI to specific value streams and control owners rather than reasoning about the bank in the abstract.

business_context.headline: Regulated regional bank, broad lines, thin outcome evidence
business_context.narrative: FS Demo operates as a multi-line regulated bank spanning consumer and commercial banking, cards and payments, wealth, treasury, and financial crimes under strong supervisory oversight. The enterprise profile is a synthetic demonstration set and must be validated against real financials and operating data before advisory use. Metrics exist by name across benefit, cycle-time, control-pressure, adoption, and unit-cost families, but none are finance-approved, so the bank knows what it wants to measure without yet being able to measure it.

operating_model.headline: Clear functions, unresolved data and model accountability
operating_model.narrative: The functional and divisional map is well articulated, and application owners and initiative sponsors are named. The gap is not who runs systems but who owns data products, model risk, and control attestation — those decision rights are not yet assigned across key domains. Workforce beneficiaries such as fraud analysts, AML investigators, loan officers, and contact-center agents are identifiable, but their readiness for AI-changed workflows is not evidenced.

capabilities.headline: Strong capability intent, limited cross-domain data sharing
capabilities.narrative: Lending, fraud, AML/KYC, payments, and wealth operate as distinct capabilities with limited cross-domain data sharing. The capability ambitions — Customer 360, real-time fraud, AML monitoring, contact-center assist, credit automation — are coherent and industry-aligned. Their realization depends on shared, certified data that does not yet flow across these functions.

value_streams.headline: Value hypotheses named, baselines and value evidence absent
value_streams.narrative: Value streams are expressed through eighteen named initiatives with headline value signals, but promised value is not yet reconciled to measured value and no baseline is finance-approved. Leadership can direct which streams to prioritize, but cannot yet claim realized benefit. The immediate task is baseline agreement on the two or three streams chosen for production.

applications_context.headline: Broad estate, fully owned, integration evidence incomplete
applications_context.narrative: The application estate is broad across core banking, cards, payments, AML/fraud, and risk, and every application carries a named owner captured on the source record. Ownership completeness is a genuine strength. The open question is integration and lineage maturity between these platforms, which remains incomplete and gates the foundation initiatives.

data_context.headline: Data ambitions ahead of ownership and lineage
data_context.narrative: Customer 360, a certified semantic layer, and cross-domain data products are named ambitions, but data-product ownership and lineage evidence are not yet established. Identity and semantic foundations are aspirational rather than certified. Without them, downstream AI workflows inherit unmanaged data risk.

technology_context.headline: Lakehouse and 360 foundation aspirational, not evidenced
technology_context.narrative: Cloud lakehouse and Customer 360 foundations are described as target state; current infrastructure evidence is not yet validated. Architecture dependencies across applications, data, and platforms carry incomplete integration evidence. Technology lifecycle and vendor-linked platform risk need to be materialized before foundation programs can be underwritten.

vendor_context.headline: Vendor-rich estate, obligations not yet linked
vendor_context.narrative: The bank depends on a wide set of core, cards, payments, and financial-crimes vendors. SLA obligations, invoice variances, and exit-right gaps exist but are not linked to the systems and workflows they support. Managed-services scope is identified but its accountability boundaries are unconfirmed.

risk_context.headline: Controls present but disconnected from certified data
risk_context.narrative: Regulatory-reporting, AML-reviewer, and fair-lending controls are identified but not linked to certified data products or the systems that feed them. Structural constraints — infrastructure, data, and vendor exposure — compound the control gap. This disconnection is the central obstacle to passing a model-risk gate.

portfolio_context.headline: Full pipeline, no finance-approved value case
portfolio_context.narrative: The initiative and budget picture shows an active portfolio spanning fraud, AML, contact center, credit, Customer 360, and semantic-layer foundations, with a run/change and capex/opex split available at medium confidence. Promised value is documented; measured value and finance-approved baselines are not. Prioritization should follow evidence readiness, not headline value signals alone.

ai_opportunity_context.headline: Right AI targets, planning-grade until evidence clears
ai_opportunity_context.narrative: AI use cases are correctly aimed at fraud, AML, SAR drafting, contact-center assist, and credit spreading — the standard high-value regulated-bank plays. All remain planning-grade pending confirmation of data, systems, controls, owners, and value evidence. Industry patterns require model-risk, lineage, and reviewer controls before any of these scale.

evidence_context.headline: Evidence exists but is low-specificity and unowned
evidence_context.narrative: Evidence sources are largely directional or not-evidenced, with unnamed owners and generic locators. Expert lenses across model risk, AML compliance, fair lending, and data governance each surface distinct but compounding blockers. The evidence spine must be strengthened with source-owner validation before board-grade claims are possible.

relationships_context.headline: Rich relationship map connecting owners, systems, initiatives
relationships_context.narrative: Relationship evidence links functions, systems, vendors, sponsors, and initiatives, including sponsor and data-owner dependencies for named programs. This is the strongest-materialized dimension and lets the bank reason across the estate. It also reveals where initiatives depend on change adoption, data-owner signoff, and readiness that are not yet in place.

The initiative pipeline correctly targets fraud, financial crimes, and contact-center assist — the highest-value regulated-bank plays — so selection risk is low and effort should shift to evidence and sequencing.

decisions.statement: Narrow the eighteen-initiative book to two or three evidence-backed workflows — anchored on fraud and AML — and fund those to production.
Assign a named data-product owner, model-risk owner, and control attestor for each production candidate before any scale decision.
Require a Finance-agreed baseline for each prioritized workflow as a condition of continued funding.
Sequence payments and Customer 360 programs explicitly behind certification of their core, sanctions, and lineage dependencies.

recommendations.statement: Stand up a model-risk and data-product accountability spine as the first workstream, since it gates every downstream production move.
Link existing controls to certified data products and systems so AI-assisted decisions are demonstrably governed for supervisors.
Connect vendor obligations to the critical workflows they support to recover renewal leverage and manage concentration risk.
Use the relationship spine to validate sponsor, owner, and dependency readiness for the two or three prioritized workflows before committing delivery.

open_questions.statement: Which two or three workflows will leadership commit to as the production proof set, and who sponsors each?
What are the current false-positive, cycle-time, and handle-time baselines Finance will accept for fraud, AML, and contact-center workflows?
Who will own data products and model risk for each candidate, and against what attestation standard?
What is the certified integration and lineage state of core, payments, and sanctions platforms that foundation initiatives depend on?
Which vendor contracts carry near-term renewal or exit-right exposure against critical workflows?

quality_notes: Business-outcome-first synthesis; technical foundations (lakehouse, semantic layer, integration) framed only where the business gate justifies them.
No raw inventory narrated as value; application count converted to ownership-coverage language and initiative book to portfolio-narrowing decisions.

evidence_status set to not_evidenced across conclusions because evidence_index entries are low-specificity placeholders insufficient for the specific claims; no citation-shaped IDs cited without support.
industry_comparison uses only the genuinely relevant fact-base patterns (model-risk gate, payments dependency, AML false-positive, comparable play 1); generic placeholder plays skipped.
Shared conclusions written once and tagged via applies_to_dimensions to prevent drift (e.g. ownership coverage across apps/org/tech_lifecycle).
material_gaps and material_advantages held to 5 and 4 items respectively — only differences that change a leadership decision.

client_visible.reason: The enterprise book is business-first, coherent, and disciplined about not narrating raw inventory as value, and its classification posture is honest. However, the assembled dimension pack carries several structural gaps that a deterministic validator will reject before human review. The enterprise_thesis dimension is entirely empty of headline, takeaway, and insights. Multiple dimensions carry visual_binding specifications that omit the mandated visual contract fields, and no dimension expresses a rendered relationship_graph contract even though graph_binding data is present. Content-classification and evidence-maturity/business-object-classification fields required on client-visible claims and business objects are absent throughout the dimension layer. These are correctable structural completeness issues rather than narrative-quality concerns, so the pack should be revised and re-passed rather than approved as-is.

violations.detail: The enterprise_thesis dimension returns empty headline, executive_takeaway, key_insights, strategic_implication, and confidence_statement. The lead dimension of the book cannot render and must be populated from the executive_narrative.

Chart visual_bindings specify visual_type, title, and a data query but omit the mandated chart-visual fields executive_question, classification, data_points, encoding, annotation, evidence_boundary, and empty_state. A chart visual must carry all of these before it can render.

Each graph_binding supplies projection and relationship metadata but no relationship_graph visual contract. A relationship_graph requires visual_type, projection_type, classification, node_groups, edge_meaning, layout_hint, visual_emphasis, and empty_state; none are present. Raw node_count and edge_count are also carried and must not surface as executive value.

Client-visible insights, gaps, advantages, and actions across all dimensions carry evidence_status but no content classification field. Every client-visible claim must carry exactly one classification from the content enum; this is absent at the dimension layer.

Dimensions that surface use-case and business-object claims (fraud, AML, contact-center assist, Customer 360, semantic layer) do not attach evidence_maturity or business_object_classification. Use cases and foundations must be distinguished so the semantic layer and Customer 360 are marked as strategic_foundation rather than qualified_use_case, and fraud/AML workflows are marked directional qualified_use_case candidates.
node_count 66 and edge_count 40 are carried on graph bindings. These must be translated into coverage or dependency-density language and never rendered as executive value cards.

quality_notes: Enterprise book (pass 01) is business-outcome-first and does not lead with lakehouse/semantic-layer technology; foundations are framed only where a business gate justifies them.
No raw inventory narrated as value at the book level; application and initiative counts converted to ownership-coverage and portfolio-narrowing language.
Classification posture in the book is honest: not_evidenced applied across conclusions where evidence is low-specificity, and confidence tags map to the content enum.
No tenant leakage of internal aliases as executive claims; FS Demo used as display name consistently.

Foundation vs use-case discipline is correct in the book narrative (semantic layer and Customer 360 treated as foundations), but not yet enforced with business_object_classification at the dimension layer.

Primary structural defects are in the assembled dimension layer: one empty lead dimension, chart visual contracts missing required fields, and relationship_graph contracts absent despite graph bindings.
Approval prose avoids reserved severity words; severity language confined to violation objects.

enterprise_story_integrated.title: FS Demo: Evidence Before Activation — Turning a Loaded Estate into a Governed AI Portfolio
enterprise_story_integrated.thesis: FS Demo has assembled the raw material for a bank-wide AI program — a fully-owned application estate, a rich book of regulated functions, and eighteen named initiatives with headline value signals — but almost none of it is yet finance-approved or control-linked. The governing argument is that the constraint on value is not idea supply; it is evidence, ownership, and control linkage. Leadership should treat the next two quarters as an evidence-and-accountability sprint that converts a directional portfolio into two or three defensible, in-production workflows, rather than launching the full slate at once.
enterprise_story_integrated.narrative_arc: The enterprise is a regulated, multi-line regional bank operating consumer and commercial banking, cards and payments, wealth, treasury, and financial crimes under strong oversight. Its technology estate is broad and, unusually, every application carries a named owner. Yet the initiative book — fraud, AML triage, SAR drafting, contact-center assist, credit spreading, Customer 360 — sits at planning-grade with no baselines, no realized savings, and no line to certified data products or controls. Industry patterns for regulated banking make the sequence unambiguous: model-risk gating, lineage, and reviewer controls come before scale. FS Demo is ahead on ownership hygiene and idea generation but behind on the evidence and control spine that lets any of these move to production. The path forward narrows the slate, assigns data-product and model accountability, and proves value on the fraud and AML workflows where the industry pattern and internal signal both point.
strategic_agenda: Narrow eighteen initiatives to two or three evidence-backed workflows and fund those to production.
Assign data-product ownership, model-risk accountability, and control attestation for every candidate before scale.
Establish finance-approved baselines so headline value signals become defensible business cases.
Sequence payments and Customer 360 work behind their core and lineage dependencies rather than in parallel.
strategic_tensions: Broad idea pipeline and headline value versus zero finance-approved baselines to defend any of it.
Complete application ownership versus unassigned data-product, model, and control accountability.
Pressure to demonstrate AI breadth versus regulatory requirement to gate on model risk and lineage first.

Each graph_binding supplies projection and relationship metadata but no relationship_graph visual contract. A relationship_graph requires visual_type, projection_type, classification, node_groups, edge_meaning, layout_hint, visual_emphasis, and empty_state; none are present. Raw node_count and edge_count are also carried and must not surface as executive value.

Client-visible insights, gaps, advantages, and actions across all dimensions carry evidence_status but no content classification field. Every client-visible claim must carry exactly one classification from the content enum; this is absent at the dimension layer.

Dimensions that surface use-case and business-object claims (fraud, AML, contact-center assist, Customer 360, semantic layer) do not attach evidence_maturity or business_object_classification. Use cases and foundations must be distinguished so the semantic layer and Customer 360 are marked as strategic_foundation rather than qualified_use_case, and fraud/AML workflows are marked directional qualified_use_case candidates.
